children: will be reporting results this Monday after the bell. Here’s what you need to know.

Qualys beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $182.2 million, up 11% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a solid beat of analysts’ billings estimates and an impressive beat of analysts’ adjusted operating income estimates.
Is Qualys a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Qualys’s revenue to grow 9.9% year on year, in line with the 10.4% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Qualys has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at Qualys’s peers in the cybersecurity segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Tenable delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 9.5%, beating analysts’ expectations by 1.8%, and Rapid7 reported a revenue decline of 2.5%, topping estimates by 1.6%. Tenable traded up 6.3% following the results while Rapid7 was also up 2.7%.

Investors in the cybersecurity segment have had fairly steady hands going into earnings, with share prices down 1.4% on average over the last month. Qualys is down 6.1% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $187.59 (compared to the current share price of $190.12).
